# How Far You Have Come {background-color="#D9DBDB"}

## When You Started This Module...

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column}

### Then

- Could fit data to a spreadsheet and run a t-test
- Produced plots to describe a dataset
- Understood statistical significance in an inferential framework
- Worked entirely within a single script with no version history

:::

::: {.column}

### Now

- Build reproducible, documented analysis pipelines in R
- Evaluate predictive models on held-out test data
- Version control your work with GitHub
- Critically assess whether a complex model is justified
- Use AI tools as a thinking partner, not an answer machine

:::

::::

::: {.fragment}
**The shift is not in the software. It is in how you think about data.**
:::


# What You Have Covered {background-color="#D9DBDB"}

## Topics Across the Module

| Theme | Topics |
|---|---|
| **Foundations** | Coding practice, code review & readability, GitHub for version control, AI pair programming |
| **Data & Design** | Data visualisation, experimental design, power analysis, introduction to causal inference |
| **Statistical Modelling** | Linear models, generalised linear models, mixed models |
| **Machine Learning** | Ridge regression, logistic regression, random forests, PCA, k-means clustering |


# The Thinking Behind It All {background-color="#D9DBDB"}

## How Good Data Science Works

These are habits, not just skills.

:::{.incremental}

- **Write code for the next person** — including future you; clarity is not optional

- **Evaluate before you interpret** — never report a coefficient without checking model assumptions first

- **Complexity requires justification** — a simpler model that performs equally well is always preferable

- **Be honest about poor performance** — a modest result from a limited dataset is a result, not a failure

- **Document and version everything** — reproducibility is a scientific standard, not a courtesy

:::

::: {.fragment}
Science that cannot be reproduced is not science.
:::


# How It All Connects {background-color="#D9DBDB"}

## One Workflow. Every Question.

```{r fig-connections, fig.height=7, fig.width=10}

pal <- c(
  foundations = "#D9DBDB",
  data_design = "#E9C46A",
  stats       = "#457B9D",
  ml          = "#2a9d8f"
)

nodes <- tribble(
  ~label,                          ~x,    ~y,    ~group,
  "Coding &\ncode review",          1.0,   4.5,   "foundations",
  "Version control\n(GitHub)",      2.5,   4.5,   "foundations",
  "AI pair\nprogramming",           4.0,   4.5,   "foundations",
  "Data\nvisualisation",            1.0,   3.0,   "data_design",
  "Experimental design\n& power",   2.5,   3.0,   "data_design",
  "Causal\ninference",              4.0,   3.0,   "data_design",
  "Linear\nmodels",                 1.0,   1.5,   "stats",
  "GLMs",                           2.5,   1.5,   "stats",
  "Mixed\nmodels",                  4.0,   1.5,   "stats",
  "Ridge\nregression",              0.5,   0.0,   "ml",
  "Logistic\nregression",           1.9,   0.0,   "ml",
  "Random\nforests",                3.2,   0.0,   "ml",
  "PCA &\nclustering",              4.6,   0.0,   "ml"
) |>
  mutate(
    fill     = pal[group],
    text_col = if_else(group %in% c("stats", "ml"), "white", "grey20")
  )

hw <- 0.55
hh <- 0.38

ggplot() +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -0.2, xmax = 5.4,
           ymin =  4.05, ymax = 4.95, fill = "#D9DBDB", alpha = 0.35) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -0.2, xmax = 5.4,
           ymin =  2.55, ymax = 3.45, fill = "#E9C46A", alpha = 0.35) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -0.2, xmax = 5.4,
           ymin =  1.05, ymax = 1.95, fill = "#457B9D", alpha = 0.25) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -0.2, xmax = 5.4,
           ymin = -0.45, ymax = 0.45, fill = "#2a9d8f", alpha = 0.25) +
  annotate("segment",
           x = 2.5, xend = 2.5, y = 4.05, yend = 3.45,
           arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm"), type = "closed"),
           colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.7) +
  annotate("segment",
           x = 2.5, xend = 2.5, y = 2.55, yend = 1.95,
           arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm"), type = "closed"),
           colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.7) +
  annotate("segment",
           x = 2.5, xend = 2.5, y = 1.05, yend = 0.45,
           arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm"), type = "closed"),
           colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_rect(data = nodes,
            aes(xmin = x - hw, xmax = x + hw,
                ymin = y - hh, ymax = y + hh,
                fill = fill),
            colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  geom_text(data = nodes,
            aes(x = x, y = y, label = label, colour = text_col),
            size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", lineheight = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  annotate("text", x = 5.5, y = 4.5, label = "FOUNDATIONS",
           hjust = 0, size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", colour = "grey40") +
  annotate("text", x = 5.5, y = 3.0, label = "DATA & DESIGN",
           hjust = 0, size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", colour = "grey40") +
  annotate("text", x = 5.5, y = 1.5, label = "STATISTICAL\nMODELLING",
           hjust = 0, size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", colour = "grey40",
           lineheight = 0.85) +
  annotate("text", x = 5.5, y = 0.0, label = "MACHINE\nLEARNING",
           hjust = 0, size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", colour = "grey40",
           lineheight = 0.85) +
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1, xlim = c(-0.3, 8.0), ylim = c(-0.7, 5.2)) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    plot.margin     = margin(15, 15, 15, 15)
  )
```


# Where Could This Take You? {background-color="#D9DBDB"}

## Pathways From Here

| Pathway | What it involves |
|---|---|
| **Your final year research project** | Apply these tools directly to your own data — talk to your supervisor about where ML or reproducible pipelines could strengthen your project |
| **BIO6XXX Bioinformatics (Level 6)** | Builds on GLMs, PCA, and ML to add sequence analysis, genome assembly, and Bioconductor tools including DESeq2 and limma |
| **MSc Computational Biology / Bioinformatics** | Full pipeline from raw sequencing data to biological inference; the modelling and reproducibility skills from this module are direct entry requirements |
| **Independent learning** | See Blackboard |


# Keep Learning {background-color="#D9DBDB"}

## Resources to Take Away

**Modelling & machine learning**

- [Tidy Modelling with R](https://www.tmwr.org) — Kuhn & Silge; open access; direct extension of this module
- [An Introduction to Statistical Learning](https://www.statlearning.com) — James et al.; R edition; free PDF
- [StatQuest with Josh Starmer](https://www.youtube.com/@statquest) — conceptual foundations without assumed mathematics background

**Bioinformatics**

- [Bioconductor workflows](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/workflows) — curated end-to-end pipelines for RNA-seq, single-cell, and more
